description.invocation: torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 gpt2_ddp_training.py --output <run-dir> --profile (from the repository root; --warmup/--repeats default to 2/5). One measured unit = one full accumulated training step from the stored initial weights: reset() restores the seeded initial state_dict, accumulate() runs 4 microbatches of per-rank GPU-resident synthetic input_ids (micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, generator seed 31000+rank) with loss divided by accumulation_steps and DDP no_sync() on the first 3 microbatches so the gradient allreduce runs only in the 4th backward, then optimizer.step() (SGD lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False) and torch.cuda.synchronize(). Unit outputs: finite summed FP32 loss, allreduced gradients, updated FP32 parameters. notes: Command provenance: intent.json command 'torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 gpt2_ddp_training.py --output /tmp/original-ddp --profile'; warmup=2 and repeats=5 come from common.py:24-25 defaults, which the command does not override.

Objective definition (workloads.json communication_metric_caveat, README line 48): per-rank sum of device NCCL kernel durations over the whole accumulated step, including device waiting; NOT wire time, critical-path time or exposed communication. Maximum across ranks, sampled in 3 separately profiled diagnostic invocations (gpt2_ddp_training.py:121-125) and reduced by median (sorted(values)[1], gpt2_ddp_training.py:156-157) - hence rank_aggregation=max with aggregation_order=ranks_then_samples.

The source metric diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms (computed by common.py profile_once nccl_kernel_sum_ms from CUDA traces) maps to the installed collector torch_communication.communication_kernel_sum_ms per deployment.json metric_collectors; make_project_requests.py:51-55 uses the same mapping for this exact goal. Collector availability is verified by the actual workload worker.

Step-time constraint from workloads.json:30 step_ms_max_baseline_ratio=1.05 on the communication goal: clean step_ms (per-repeat maximum across rank-local step times, median of 5 repeats; gpt2_ddp_training.py:148-152 with common.py:66-71 summarize) must stay <= 1.05x baseline. Gloo control-group barrier and reset() are outside the timed boundary (gpt2_ddp_training.py:112-118).

Discrete exact comparisons that must hold: every parameter gradient bitwise identical across ranks (torch.testing.assert_close atol=0.0, rtol=0.0; gpt2_ddp_training.py:81-86); summed loss finite (gpt2_ddp_training.py:65); negative control must reject a +1-corrupted gradient (common.py:79-84).

Full correctness checks retained per the goal: rank-0 serial single-GPU reference consuming the identical global batch (all ranks' seeded inputs concatenated, effective batch 8) with gradient comparison before step and parameter comparison after SGD step at grad/parameter tolerances (gpt2_ddp_training.py:67-91). Reference construction, correctness checks, the 3 diagnostic traces and the separate allreduce-hook bucket inventory (gpt2_ddp_training.py:128-138) are measurement infrastructure, not work repeated by the adapter.

Numerics preserved end to end: FP32 weights and inputs, TF32 disabled for matmul and cudnn, float32_matmul_precision 'highest', cudnn.benchmark off, attn_implementation='eager', all dropout 0, use_cache=False (common.py:34-42; gpt2_ddp_training.py:26). Effective batch = 2*1*4 = 8; tokens per step = 2*1*128*4 = 1024.

Deterministic fixtures: model init torch.manual_seed(20261020) (gpt2_ddp_training.py:25); per-rank token inputs torch.Generator seed 31000+rank (gpt2_ddp_training.py:31-33); inputs are pre-generated and moved to device before any timing.

Baseline communication implementation to reproduce (gpt2_ddp_training.py:59-60 and :40): DDP(device_ids=[rank], broadcast_buffers=False, bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True) with no_sync() on the first accumulation_steps-1 microbatches, so one gradient allreduce per step; SGD lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0, foreach=False.

selection.rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted version (stem micro-batch rows8 + stage-0 micro-batch rows8, both verified executing in this discovery: stem Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool2d n=4, copy_ n=4, one 32x64x56x56 assembly; stage-0 slices/Sequential/Identity n=4, add_ n=8) measures exactly 177,409,024 B = live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained workspace 8,622,944 + 4 x 25,690,112, where 25,690,112 is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 unit (also exactly 8x64x112x112). The previous parameter search measured stage0_chunk_rows=8 and =16 at the identical 177,409,024, so the binding moment is independent of stage-0 chunk transients; the peak now sits in a phase that parameter cannot touch. Static liveness bounds leave the unchanged stage-1 phase at <= base + 1 unit + 3-4 x 12,845,056 and the chunked stage-0 phase at ~ base + 2 units + 6,422,528 transients, both below the measured 4 units; the stem phase is the only phase where 3 x 25,690,112 coexist in the observed aten sequence (full assembly empty+4x copy_, chunk conv_out 8x64x112x112, chunk bn_out 8x64x112x112), with the fourth unit unexplained by static shapes (per-operator allocation attribution is an explicit unknown; plausibly cudnn workspace for the 7x7 stride-2 conv, which also scales with chunk rows). Halving the stem chunk is the one lever that shrinks every term of that phase: rows=4 turns conv_out/bn_out (and any row-scaled workspace) into 12,845,056 each while the assembly stays 25,690,112. The earlier stem parameter search already executed rows=4 cleanly (objective identical to rows=8 at 203,099,136 while stage 0 was binding), so the lever is proven executable and quality-passing. Selection: region scope re-binding the ResNetEmbeddings boundary (call d16297b8a11b79a2657853d0) with the same proven pattern at half chunk size, running the unchanged Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/max_pool parents through context.references on contiguous row chunks and assembling one [32,64,56,56] FP32 tensor consumed unchanged by the untouched stage-0 bundle and stages 1-3; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies. All 32 stem-subtree groups are selected; the 49 additional calls (stage-0 assembly empty/copy_/slice calls and 43 record_function_exit family calls) are included only because those group families share ownership across the region boundary, matching the accepted region-selection precedent.
selection.hypothesis: Re-binding the stem region at chunk_rows=4 (parameter space may probe 2/4/8) lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 177,409,024 B to approximately 151,718,912 B (-25,690,112, -14.5%): with 4-row chunks the stem-phase coexistence becomes assembly 25,690,112 + conv_out 12,845,056 + bn_out 12,845,056 + one further <=25,690,112 term (the statically unexplained unit, likely conv workspace that itself shrinks with rows), i.e. base 74,648,576 + 2 x 25,690,112 + 2 x 12,845,056 at worst. Even if the unexplained unit is fixed-size, the arithmetic lands exactly on 151,718,912; the graceful floor is the unchanged stage-0 phase (~145.3 MB: stage input + assembled output + 6,422,528 transients) and stage-1 phase (~151.4 MB), so no gain below ~145 MB is claimed. Throughput: constraint is images_per_second >= 7,158.9 (0.95 x 7535.66); the accepted version measured 8,506-8,538 img/s (16-19% headroom), rows=4 only adds four extra small conv/bn/relu/pool launches versus the accepted rows=8 route, and stem chunking has previously measured throughput-neutral, so the constraint is expected to hold. Numerics: identical per-sample FP32 kernels (eval batch_norm, out-of-place relu, max_pool2d, conv2d) on contiguous batch slices, the pattern already accepted twice with max_abs_error 7.6e-06 within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1; full 1000-class logits and predicted classes are unchanged. These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean paired measurement.

selection.rationale: Objective is peak_allocated_bytes (baseline 280,169,472 B, median of clean samples) with images_per_second >= 0.95x7535.66 = 7158.9. The peak decomposes exactly from the measured assets: live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + conv1 output 32x64x112x112x4 = 102,760,448 coexisting with the out-of-place batch_norm1 output of the same size + 8,622,944 workspace = 280,169,472 exactly. That coexistence happens inside ResNetEmbeddings (model.resnet.embedder): the stem's two 112x112x64 tensors are 73% of the peak. Note the separately observed ReLU duplication (all 17 ReLUs out-of-place) is not the binding term: the ReLU moment is also a 2x102,760,448 coexistence, so in-place ReLU alone cannot move the peak; the conv->BN output coexistence is the floor that must be attacked. Selection: the stem region (ResNetEmbeddings module and its subtree: stem ResNetConvLayer 0022893ec8c1ceea869f with the single target model.resnet.embedder.embedder, its Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU modules, and the MaxPool2d pooler). The candidate replaces the ResNetEmbeddings forward (module boundary, children invoked through context.references; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies) to micro-batch the stem along the frozen batch dimension: 4 contiguous chunks of 8 rows, each chunk running the unchanged conv1 -> bn1(eval) -> relu1 -> maxpool path on a contiguous slice (no copies), with chunk outputs assembled into the same [32,64,56,56] hidden state (25,690,112 B) for the untouched stages. All inherited stem calls still execute (4x per invocation), preserving quality coverage without CUDA-graph replay. Region scope because every call in the stem subtree changes execution (invocation count 1->4, per-call batch 32->8); all 17 observed stem-subtree calls are listed, including the aten conv2d/batch_norm/relu/max_pool2d calls and the discovery record_function hooks that will fire per chunk. No calls outside the region are affected: stage 0+ receive the same-shape, same-value hidden state through the same ops. Rejected alternatives: whole-model micro-batching (execution_plan) would cut deeper (~122 MB) but re-times all 20 convs (~4156 us of diagnostic CUDA time) at batch 8 and risks the 7158.9 img/s floor; deduplicating the 3 unique input images contradicts the frozen batch-32 workload (all 32 rows must execute); CUDA-graph replay skips Python hooks and breaks coverage per binding-contract; folding BN into conv weights changes parameter values (invariant); in-place ReLU alone does not move the 2-tensor peak. Throughput safety: the stem is 907.7/4156.2 us (21.8%) of diagnostic CUDA time, and its kernels are bandwidth-bound on the 112x112x64 tensors - bn_fw_inf_1C11_NCHW 227.2 us, clamp/relu 217.8 us, max_pool_forward_nchw 198.7 us - whose grids stay far above SM saturation at batch 8 and whose total bytes moved are unchanged; only conv1's scudnn kernel (262.5 us) can lose modest efficiency, so even a 20% stem slowdown keeps wall time <= ~4.42 ms (>= ~7240 img/s).
selection.hypothesis: Chunking the stem 4x8 lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 280,169,472 B to approximately 143-152 MB (-46% to -49%). With batch-8 chunks the stem transient becomes params 46,758,048 + input 19,267,584 + assembled stem output 25,690,112 + one chunk's conv_out + bn_out coexistence 2x25,690,112 (+ small workspaces) = 143,095,968 + ws, which matches the new binding tier set outside the region by stage 0's out-of-place conv coexistence (input 25,690,112 + conv_out + bn_out), the eager-execution floor reachable without editing stage semantics. If measurement shows batch-8 chunks cost more than the 5% throughput budget, 2x16 chunks inside the same region still yield ~168.8 MB + ws (-38% to -40%); chunk size is tunable within this one boundary. Expected images_per_second 7300-7500 (>= 7158.9) since the bandwidth-bound stem kernels move identical total bytes at near-identical efficiency; expected numerics unchanged: identical aten kernels on contiguous batch slices, BN(eval)/ReLU/MaxPool per-sample exact, conv1 at worst reduction-order-level differences far below the atol=rtol=1e-4 logits tolerance, preserving exact top-1. These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean timing, peak and quality checks.

selection.rationale: Objective peak_allocated_bytes on the current accepted version measures 203,099,136 B (previous-feedback project_measurement candidate_values, both AB/BA endpoints, zero noise). That peak decomposes exactly as live FP32 params 46,758,048 + GPU-resident input 19,267,584 + retained cudnn workspace 8,622,944 + 5 x 25,690,112 = 128,450,560, where 25,690,112 is one 32x64x56x56 FP32 activation. Tensors of that shape exist only in encoder stage 0 (model.resnet.encoder.stages.0: two ResNetBasicLayers at 64ch/56x56) and its input (the stem output), so the binding memory tier is stage 0's full-batch activation coexistence, not the already-optimized stem: parameter search showed stem chunk 4 and 8 both measure exactly 203,099,136 (stem not binding), while chunk 16 rises to 205,196,288 (stem-limited), and per aten::add_/relu/batch_norm evidence in calls.json stage 0 runs out-of-place conv->bn chains plus out-of-place post-add nn.ReLU(inplace=False) around an in-place residual add. The accepted stem micro-batch is verified executing in the current revision (trace: embedder convolution/normalization/activation/max_pool2d n=4, 8 slice.Tensor, empty+copy_ assembly; coverage route stem_microbatch_rows8 with reference invocations 8/8), so a stage-0 edit composes on top of it and the stem tier (~151.7 MB) becomes the post-edit floor. Selection: region scope replacing the stages.0 module boundary (call 595c8331c60823c132ca3a4a) with the same proven pattern - run the unchanged two BasicLayer parents (f3ec7e68beb5e3d3f846d2fa, dfb96bb329e6c3859d690b9a) through context.references on contiguous row chunks of the frozen batch-32 input and assemble chunk results into one [32,64,56,56] tensor for the untouched later stages; no functional dispatch sites, so the legacy direct-callable backend applies. All 72 observed calls in the stages.0 subtree are affected (module, aten and record_function hook invocation counts change 1->4); four stages.1-family calls (47f42cfd2d55620ecd13e733, b92e9ace8737abe290b03c62, ae6782daa6589784cea3aad8, 6d17e25a4f8679b7b8f3d445) are included only because current group families share ownership across stages.0/stages.1; their own execution is unchanged. No call outside this region changes: stem, pooler, classifier and stages.1-3 run exactly as in the accepted version.
selection.hypothesis: Micro-batching stage 0 into 4 chunks of 8 rows lowers peak_allocated_bytes from 203,099,136 B to approximately 151.7 MB (-25%): with batch-8 chunks the stage-0 moment becomes stem output 25,690,112 + assembled stage-0 output 25,690,112 + chunk transients 4 x 6,422,528 = 3 x 25,690,112 total coexistence, matching the tier the unchanged stem (input 19,267,584 + output 25,690,112 + 2 chunk transients) and unchanged stage 1 (stage-0 output 25,690,112 + 4 x 12,845,056) already set at ~151,718,912 B. One 25,690,112 term in the current peak (5 vs the 4 coexisting activations visible in the aten call sequence) is not fully explained by static call-shape analysis, so the honest pessimistic bound is 177,409,024 B (-12.7%); the 4-vs-8-chunk stem equivalence shows such tier plateaus are real and measurable. Throughput: ~0.5 ms headroom exists (accepted version 3.92-3.96 ms, 8079-8121 img/s vs floor 7158.9 = 4.47 ms); stem chunking at batch 8 measured faster than baseline, and stage 0 adds ~54 launches of already-warmed kernels, so images_per_second >= 7158.9 is expected to hold, with a chunk_rows=16 variant inside the same boundary (~177.4 MB peak) as fallback. Numerics: identical aten kernels on contiguous batch slices; eval BatchNorm, out-of-place ReLU and the in-place residual add are per-sample exact, so logits stay within atol=rtol=1e-4 and top-1 stays exact, as the accepted stem micro-batch already demonstrated (max_abs_error 0.0). These benefit, throughput and numerics expectations are hypotheses to be tested by the evaluator's clean timing, peak and quality checks.
